THE MECHANISM
You're not confused about who's choosing you.
You're measuring the wrong thing.

You've built a whole private practice around it — timing replies, re-reading tone, tracking read receipts. What you're actually running is intensity instead of consistency.

WHY UNAVAILABLE FEELS BIGGER
Their approval costs more.
So you price it higher.

Anything out of reach gets a premium — it's not that they're more valuable, it's that scarcity reads as value. Watch what happens when they finally text back: the heat drops out in weeks. You never wanted them. You wanted the open loop to close.

WHAT REAL CARE ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE
Real care has no signal spike.

They check in. They show up before you ask. No drama, no waiting. Your nervous system is tuned to notice change, so "steady" reads as "nothing happening."

Words are cheap.
Actions are the data.

THE BILL NOBODY TALKS ABOUT
While you chased, the real ones kept extending — quietly.

They asked how you were. They noticed you were off. You gave them the leftovers. They felt it. So they extended a little less. Nobody grieves the friendships they let starve — we just call it drift.

THE NUMBERS, FINALLY RUN RIGHT
Six months auditing one person's silence for meaning.

Zero minutes noticing my friend had shown up for everything — without ever being asked.

THE ACTUAL TAKEAWAY
Not being someone's priority is information about them. Not a verdict on you.

The work isn't chasing harder. It's building a sense of worth that doesn't need a co-signer. Do that, and the people who were always there stop being background. They didn't change. Your instrument did.
